# Men’s March Madness Sets Opening-Day Viewership Record

Thursday’s TV coverage averaged a record 9.1 million viewers, up 6% from 2024.

By [Jeff Benson](https://frontofficesports.com/author/jbensonwrites/ "Posts by Jeff Benson")

Mar 21, 2025 | 07:12 pm

![Image 2: Mar 20, 2025; Providence, RI, USA; Arkansas Razorbacks forward Karter Knox (11) controls the ball against Kansas Jayhawks during the first half at Amica Mutual Pavilion.](https://frontofficesports.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/USATSI_25724626-scaled.jpg?quality=80&w=1024)

Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images

Want more from Front Office Sports   
in your search results?

[Add Front Office Sports on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=frontofficesports.com)

March Madness has barely begun, and it’s already setting records.

Thursday was the most-watched opening day of the NCAA men’s college basketball tournament ever, according to [preliminary Nielsen data](https://x.com/MM_MBB_TV/status/1903192914223652951). TV coverage across CBS, TNT, TBS, and truTV averaged 9.1 million viewers, up 6% from last year.

Viewership shot up further during primetime, averaging 12.2 million viewers to set a first-round record. For context, that’s more than the [first _semifinal_ game](https://www.sportsmediawatch.com/ncaa-final-four-ratings-history-most-watched-games-cbs-tbs-nbc/)each of the last four years.

The record Round of 64 numbers come on the heels of a historic First Four on Tuesday night: TruTV drew 2.2 million viewers for North Carolina’s blowout of San Diego State, while Alabama State–Saint Francis took in another 1.4 million. The combined 3.6 million viewers was a [record for a Tuesday First Four](https://frontofficesports.com/uncs-first-four-win-delivers-record-ratings-for-march-madness-opener/), up 21% from last year.

During the Round of 64, CBS Sports and TNT Sports typically share viewing figures based on viewing windows, or time slots, rather than individual games. But the broadcasters pointed out in a [social media post](https://x.com/MM_MBB_TV/status/1903192914223652951) that primetime coverage was “led by” No. 10 seed Arkansas’s 79–72 upset of No. 7 Kansas. While the Razorbacks and Jayhawks both ended the season outside the AP Top 25 rankings, the game represented a marquee matchup because of head coaches John Calipari and Bill Self. The pair have three NCAA championships and 10 Final Four appearances between them.

When the dust settles, Friday may set even more records. Duke, which is favored to win the entire tournament, took the floor Friday against No. 16 seed Mount Saint Mary’s. The Blue Devils are led by projected No. 1 NBA draft pick Cooper Flagg, who scored 14 points and grabbed 7 rebounds in the 93–49 win after [missing two games](https://frontofficesports.com/cooper-flagg-is-cleared-to-play-boosting-dukes-ncaa-title-hopes/) of the ACC tournament with an ankle injury. With Flagg, the Blue Devils have been must-see-TV, featuring in four of the 10 [most-watched regular-season games](https://frontofficesports.com/a-march-madness-ratings-resurgence-may-depend-on-cooper-flagg/) this season.

While Thursday’s figures are expected to go up when final numbers are released, they do come with an asterisk. Nielsen changed how it tracks out-of-home (OOH) audiences (people who watch games in bars or restaurants, for example) [earlier this year](https://frontofficesports.com/super-bowl-lix-eyes-tv-ratings-record-with-nielsen-expansion/). According to the analytics firm, it now tracks OOH audiences in 100% of the contiguous United States. In prior years, OOH audiences in at least one-third of the country—particularly rural areas—were not tracked.

# March Madness Reportedly Generates $410M of In-Game Brand Exposure

*   March Madness delivered more than $410 million worth of media value for featured brands in telecasts, according to a report.
*   NCAA corporate partners, equipment companies and apparel brands benefited the most.

By [Amanda Christovich](https://frontofficesports.com/author/amanda-christovich/ "Posts by Amanda Christovich")

Apr 05, 2022 | 04:05 pm

![Image 2](https://frontofficesports.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/FOS-22-PM-4.5-NCAA-Championship.jpg?quality=80&w=1024)

Robert Deutsch-USA TODAY Sports

Want more from Front Office Sports   
in your search results?

[Add Front Office Sports on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=frontofficesports.com)

The brands featured during this year’s NCAA Division I basketball tournaments received multimillion-dollar platforms — even outside of commercials.

Men’s and women’s March Madness delivered **more than $410 million worth of media exposure value** for featured brands in telecasts, [according](https://elevatesportsventures.com/news/marchmadness2) to a report by Elevate Sports Ventures and Hive.

That’s more than double the [delivery](https://frontofficesports.com/super-bowl-generated-170m-in-game-brand-exposure/) for **Super Bowl LVI**, which generated an estimated $170 million.

*   The companies that benefited the most included NCAA corporate sponsors, apparel brands, and equipment providers.
*   Together, **Capital One**, **Coca-Cola**, **AT&T**, **Nike**, and **Spalding**earned 56% of all media value.
*   Capital One led the women’s tournament with 13 hours and 25 minutes of exposure, while AT&T led the men’s with nine hours and 13 minutes.

In all, companies received about 187 total hours of exposure during all 134 men’s and women’s games.

A previous [report](https://frontofficesports.com/march-madness-early-rounds-generate-165m-in-brand-exposure/) noted that men’s games generate more value than women’s, as viewership numbers — and therefore the cost of a spot — is higher. This year’s women’s ratings [skyrocketed](https://frontofficesports.com/womens-march-madness-viewership-skyrockets/), with the championship game peaking at almost **6 million viewers**. It averaged 18% more than 2021, and 30% more than 2019.

### Early-Round Value

From the last day of the women’s second round onward, both tournaments generated **$245 million** in exposure. Elevate and Hive found that up to that point, $165 million had been generated.

An early-round winner for product placement was the basket stanchion arm, which helped Spalding earn the most exposure time of any brand during early rounds.

Title: Skydance Gains Full TV Control of NCAA Men’s March Madness Rights Starting in 2027

URL Source: https://cordcuttersnews.com/skydance-gains-full-tv-control-of-ncaa-mens-march-madness-rights-starting-in-2027/

Published Time: 2026-10-16T20:34:11+00:00

Markdown Content:
The newly formed Skydance media company has assumed exclusive ownership of the television, digital, and related rights to the NCAA Division I men’s basketball tournament, known as March Madness, effective for the 2027 edition and continuing through the existing contract term ending in 2032. This development follows the completion of Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery earlier this month, which combined the longtime joint rights holders—CBS Sports from the Paramount side and TNT Sports from the Warner Bros. Discovery side—under a single corporate umbrella. The combined annual rights fee for the tournament stands at approximately $1.1 billion, a figure established under the extended agreement that runs through 2032.

The shift ends a 16-year period of shared production and distribution that began with the 2011 tournament. Under the prior structure, games were split across CBS, TBS, TNT, and truTV, with all contests made available nationally and streamed via platforms associated with each partner. Early rounds featured simultaneous coverage on multiple channels, while the Final Four and national championship alternated between CBS and TBS in even- and odd-numbered years. The joint model, which originated from a 2010 agreement valued at $10.8 billion over 14 years and later extended by eight years for an additional $8.8 billion, allowed both companies to share production costs, advertising inventory, studio programming, and digital operations while ensuring every game reached viewers without regional blackouts.

The last time a single company held exclusive rights to the full NCAA men’s tournament occurred under CBS alone from 1991 through 2010. CBS first secured the rights in 1982 after outbidding NBC, which had carried the event (including the Final Four) in prior years. From 1982 to 1990, CBS shared some early-round coverage with ESPN, but beginning in 1991 it assumed sole control of the entire tournament package. That exclusive arrangement persisted until the NCAA exercised an opt-out clause after the 2010 championship and negotiated the multi-network deal with CBS and Turner Broadcasting System that launched the following year. Earlier history included limited national coverage by NBC starting in the late 1960s and various syndication arrangements before that.

Under the new Skydance structure, the company controls the full portfolio of premium sports rights that previously belonged separately to Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery. This includes agreements spanning the NFL, MLB, NHL, college conferences, and other properties, positioning Skydance as one of the largest holders of live sports media rights in the United States. For March Madness specifically, the unified ownership simplifies production decisions, advertising sales, and streaming distribution across the combined networks and platforms. The 2026 tournament, already scheduled with shared CBS and TNT Sports coverage, proceeds under the prior arrangement, while planning for 2027 and beyond consolidates under the single entity.

Industry observers note that the consolidation could influence future rights negotiations once the current deal expires after the 2032 tournament, particularly as media companies continue to balance linear television, streaming, and digital consumption of major events. The NCAA has already expanded the tournament field for the 2027 editions of both the men’s and women’s championships, a change that generates additional rights revenue under the existing agreements. Skydance’s sports leadership, drawn from the former CBS Sports operation, now oversees the combined portfolio.

The merger itself closed on October 6 after settlements resolved antitrust challenges from a group of states and the Writers Guild of America. Regulatory approvals had been secured in dozens of jurisdictions, clearing the way for the combination of studios, streaming services, networks, and sports rights. For college basketball fans, the practical result for 2027 will be continued national availability of all tournament games, now managed entirely by one company rather than a partnership between two competitors. This marks the first exclusive control by a single corporate entity since the pre-2011 CBS era and ends the unique joint-venture model that defined March Madness coverage for more than a decade and a half.
